title: The adaptive landscapes of three global Escherichia coli transcriptional regulators.
authors: Westmann, Caua Antunes; Goldbach, Leander; Wagner, Andreas
one_liner_zh: 该文通过大规模平行报告实验绘制大肠杆菌三个全局转录因子的体内调控适应度景观，聚焦TFBS序列-表达关系，但缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，且未涉及三维互作建模，仅属实验性序列功能研究。
abstract: The evolution of gene regulation is a major source of evolutionary adaptation and innovation, particularly when organisms encounter new or changing environments. Central to this process is the emergence of new transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs). Adaptive landscapes provide a powerful framework to study such emergence by linking regulatory DNA sequences to their transcriptional outputs. Although several landscapes have been characterized for DNA, RNA, and proteins, large-scale in vivo adaptive landscapes for bacterial TFBSs remain scarce. Here, we address this gap by experimentally mapping the first comprehensive in vivo regulatory landscapes for three global transcription factors in Escherichia coli: cAMP receptor protein, Fis, and IHF. Using a massively parallel reporter assay, we quantify the regulation strength of more than 30,000 TFBS variants for each factor, and reconstruct their adaptive landscapes. All three landscapes are highly rugged and exhibit pervasive epistasis, with thousands of local peaks distributed broadly across sequence space. This ruggedness contrasts sharply with the much smoother TFBS landscapes of eukaryotes. It suggests greater constraints on the evolution of prokaryotic gene regulation. Nonetheless, evolutionary simulations show that ~10% of evolving populations can reach a peak of strong regulation, a proportion that is significantly greater than in comparable random landscapes. Adaptive evolution starting from the same DNA sequence can attain different high peaks, and some peaks are reached more frequently than others. Together, our results show that de novo adaptive evolution of new gene regulation in bacteria is feasible, but subject to a blend of chance, historical contingency, and evolutionary biases.
abstract_zh: 基因调控的进化是进化适应与创新的主要来源，尤其是在生物体遭遇新环境或变化环境时。这一过程的核心是新转录因子结合位点（TFBSs）的出现。适应性景观通过将调控DNA序列与其转录输出联系起来，为研究这种出现提供了强有力的框架。尽管已有若干针对DNA、RNA和蛋白质的景观被表征，但细菌TFBS的大规模体内适应性景观仍然稀缺。在此，我们通过实验绘制了首个全面的体内调控景观，涵盖大肠杆菌中三个全局转录因子：cAMP受体蛋白、Fis和IHF。利用大规模并行报告基因分析，我们量化了每个因子超过30,000个TFBS变体的调控强度，并重建了它们的适应性景观。所有三个景观都高度崎岖，并表现出普遍的 epistasis（上位效应），在序列空间中分布着数千个局部峰。这种崎岖性与真核生物中更为平滑的TFBS景观形成鲜明对比，表明原核基因调控的进化受到更大限制。尽管如此，进化模拟显示，约10%的进化群体能够达到强调控的峰，这一比例显著高于可比随机景观中的情况。从相同DNA序列开始的适应性进化可以到达不同的高峰，且某些峰比其他峰更频繁地被达到。综合来看，我们的结果表明，细菌中新基因调控的从头适应性进化是可行的，但受制于机遇、历史偶然性和进化偏见的综合影响。
